name: aqg-memory-hygiene
description: Scan machine-local agent memory files for frontmatter schema compliance and staleness — the at-rest layer of memory hygiene, signal-only and read-only. The validate subcommand is a strict gate over each memory node's metadata frontmatter (type / status / volatility / last_verified enums, no node_type residue, superseded-pointer integrity); the staleness subcommand surfaces volatile memories whose last_verified is past a configurable horizon (default 90 days, env AQG_MEMORY_STALE_DAYS). Emits a structured report plus an exit-code gate; never mutates memory, calls audit-mcp, or touches the network — fixing stays the caller's action. Use to catch memory schema drift, an invalid or future-dated last_verified, a broken superseded pointer, or stale volatile memories needing re-verification. Complements the write-time memory-write-guard hook and the memory-hygiene discipline. Not a memory editor or coverage gate.

sentence_patterns: validate my memory files' frontmatter schema
is my agent memory schema-compliant or has it drifted?
which volatile memories are stale and need re-verification?
check the memory dir for an invalid or future-dated last_verified
did any superseded memory lose its superseded_by pointer?
run aqg-memory-hygiene validate on my project memory

cli_contract.0: success — validate all-compliant / no memory dir / empty dir; staleness always exits 0
cli_contract.1: validation failure — validate found at least one schema violation
cli_contract.2: usage error — bad args / unknown subcommand, OR PyYAML (declared dep) unavailable
cli_contract.3: reserved — config or schema error (not currently emitted)
cli_contract.70: reserved — internal error placeholder for future use

owner_only_actions: This skill is read-only / signal-only: it parses a memory dir and emits a schema + staleness report, never modifies / normalizes / supersedes / deletes any memory file (zero-write invariant test), never calls audit-mcp, never touches the network. Normalizing or superseding is the caller's action. Production / secrets / raw private data / branch protection / Owner-admin actions remain separate authorization gates.

cases.prompt: validate my agent memory files — has the frontmatter schema drifted?
which volatile memories are stale and need re-verification?
check the memory dir for an invalid or future-dated last_verified
did any superseded memory lose its superseded_by pointer or keep a node_type residue?
run /aqg-memory-hygiene validate on my project memory and show the schema report
